judgements.suggested_next_if_bad: Abandon Poole-Frenkel model. orchestrator_feedback: The ideality factor of 2.05 and symmetric-like behavior suggest that bulk-limited transport or interface recombination dominates over simple Schottky emission, so abandon pure thermionic models. The negative R² values for thermionic, TAT, and Poole-Frenkel indicate these barrier-dominated mechanisms are fundamentally mismatched to your data, while SCLC showed better log-scale fit (R²_log=0.94) but unrealistic ε_r, suggesting trap-mediated space-charge physics may be relevant if properly constrained. For ZnO with n≈2, try a two-diode model (one for interface recombination with n=2, one for bulk with n=1) or a single recombination-dominated diode with series resistance, as the near-2 ideality strongly indicates Shockley-Read-Hall recombination in the depletion region. The finite current at zero bias (J₀≈1.1 μA/cm²) requires either a shunt path or generation-recombination current component in any equivalent circuit. Consider that 200nm Au/ZnO likely has significant interface state density affecting both forward and reverse characteristics, so include interface trap states explicitly rather than trying bulk-only SCLC or barrier-only tunneling.
